sample_unit: LLM responses to viral skincare myth prompts (20 myths x 3 models)

links.outcome: Verifiability of references/citations in LLM outputs (hallucinated vs verifiable) and peer-review status
links.effect: Gemini hallucinated 62.5% of references; Perplexity reached 95.0% retrieval fidelity, yet only 19.7% of its verifiable citations were peer-reviewed, versus 76.9% (ChatGPT) and 58.3% (Gemini; p < 0.001).
links.quote: Gemini hallucinated 62.5% of references; Perplexity reached 95.0% retrieval fidelity, yet only 19.7% of its verifiable citations were peer-reviewed, versus 76.9% (ChatGPT) and 58.3% (Gemini; p < 0.001).

screen.reason: Empirical comparison of three commercial LLMs responding to viral skincare myths, evaluated by dermatologists for accuracy, safety-referral behavior, and citation hallucinations.
